Except here's a very small wrench in your gearbox to throw that whole geartrain off. When Heroes are of a particular gender, say Han Solo as a Man, or even Leia Organa as a Woman, their gender, and subsequent gender roles that they enact as part of their character, become an integral part of that character.

Who would have thought it acceptable for a guy to follow a woman halfway across the galaxy, in the name of love? If it was Solo thawing out Leia from Carbonite in Jabba's palace, the feminist harridans would be screeching about how much "that chauvanistic Solo thinks he's entitled to Leia's love, now, since he rescued the literal princess in distress". Those roles are dependent upon their gender to be funny, or endearing, as opposed to creepy or otherwise unacceptable, and changing the gender of the character, changes the Hero in question, since what the Hero has done is performed through decisions made through the lens of that gender. Mario wants to save the Princess, so he can have his "Delicious Cake" (As well as likely slake other appetites). Without that lens to view the scenario through, what motivation does Maria have to save the princess? I'm sure Cake has some motivation for Maria, but when Maria can make her own damn cake, it becomes less logical to run the gauntlet of the Koopa Corps to get it.

Thus, when Heroes have been established as a certain gender, changing that gender changes the entire concept of what the Hero is. It's no longer the hero we know and love, it's something else, something foreign...and that means evaluating it on independent grounds from our other Heroes.
